$doc: THE TYPE SYSTEM AS A TABLE. One row per level of the hierarchy, and every typographic property of every level is either a token binding or a structural keyword — there is not one raw family, size, weight, width or tracking value in this file. scripts/emit-css.mjs renders it into the `generated:typography` region of css/components.css, and scripts/build.mjs --check byte-compares the result, so the levels are the source and the CSS is the consequence. WHY THIS IS A TABLE AND NOT A COMPONENT DEFINITION. A definition describes one element's appearance and produces a React component with props; a typographic level is a utility class applied to whatever element the page already has. They also differ in a way that decides it: `.t-title` sets `line-height` TWICE, a modern value behind a fallback, and a fallback pair cannot survive translation into a class attribute — a class attribute has no order. So this layer is CSS-only by construction, which is honest, and the components pipeline stays free of a construct that only one surface could honour. WHAT IS STILL A LITERAL, AND WHY THAT IS A CONDITION RATHER THAN A PERMISSION. `line-height` and `max-width` are not bound, because neither has a token tier: line-height has twelve distinct values across nineteen declarations in the stylesheet, which is drift to be consolidated before it is tokenised rather than drift to be enshrined in tokens.json — a tier of twelve steps with one consumer each fails this system's own rule that a semantic tier earns its keep by being consumed. `max-width` here is a MEASURE, a limit on line length, which is a different job from spacing. Both are on the owner's review list, and the day either gets a tier the guard in scripts/emit-css.mjs gains a row and these become errors, exactly as font-weight and letter-spacing did in R4.

block.title: Typography scale
note: One voice per level; components and pages compose these instead
of declaring their own font stacks.
Every size here is a step of the `--text-*` ramp in tokens.json. A level
that needs its own size is a new step in the token file, not a number typed
here.
`.t-title` and `.t-statement` USED to share `--text-title`, on the argument
that they are the same level wearing different weights and cases. They are
not — they differ by SHAPE OF RESPONSE, which is the distinction the scale
now turns on. A title is a single line in a strip that has to land on the
lattice, so it steps at the grid break and the step costs nothing. A
statement is a 7-19 line paragraph in a measure, so stepping it moves it
from six lines to ten on one pixel of resize. The title steps; the statement
gets an authored curve. See the `text` $doc in tokens.json.

levels.name: display
levels.$doc: The poster voice: the display family at its widest and heaviest, uppercase, tracked in. Three sizes, and each is a step whose size is set by the WIDTH OF ITS BOX rather than by its level — which is why all three are clamps in tokens.json and why the width axis eases back at the smallest of them.

levels.name: title
levels.$doc: A section title. One level down from display in weight and width, and the only level whose leading is computed rather than chosen — it has to land on the lattice.

note: A WHOLE NUMBER OF CELLS, which is what makes the section head land — see
the `.sec__head` block. `1` was the defect: it makes the line box the font
size exactly, so the head's height was whatever the type happened to be and
landed on a lattice line only by luck.
Two declarations, not @supports: a browser without `round()` keeps 1.1,
which is no worse than the 1 it replaces. 0.8em is derived rather than
chosen — Archivo's cap height is 0.69em and capitals clear their box at
L >= 0.71F, so 0.8 has room to spare. It matters because js/main.js splits
`.sec__title` with GSAP `mask: "lines"`, which wraps every line in an
overflow:hidden box the height of its line box: too tight a box clips the
capitals permanently, and that clipping is not recoverable by scrolling.

levels.name: statement
levels.$doc: The one statement per section: display type set as a paragraph. Same weight as a title, narrower on the width axis because it runs to many lines, and it is the level that carries a measure.

levels.name: lead
levels.$doc: The reading lede. The first level that sets no family and no weight: body prose inherits both, and a level that does not change a property should not restate it.

levels.name: kicker
levels.$doc: A short qualifying line under a title. It is a colour and a measure and nothing else — the size it lands at is whatever set it.

levels.name: label
levels.$doc: The mono chrome label: the widest tracking on the ramp, uppercase, at the standard chrome step. It is the level the chip and the button are cut from, which is why those three share a family and a case.
